subject: Electrical Engineering
title: Capacitors: Storing Charge
description: A micro-lesson that makes Capacitors: Storing Charge usable.

hook.text: A camera flash takes seconds to charge but releases all its energy in a burst.

buildup.text: A capacitor stores charge on two metal plates separated by an insulator.

discovery.text: Capacitance is measured in farads. Most real caps are micro or picofarads.

twist.text: Capacitors block DC but pass AC — they charge up and stop, then reverse.

climax.text: They smooth power supplies, filter noise, and set timing in oscillators.

punchline.text: A capacitor is a tiny rechargeable bucket for electrons.

quiz.question: Why do capacitors block DC current?
options: DC has too much voltage for the plates to handle
They charge up fully and stop current once the plates reach supply voltage
The insulator between plates only conducts AC
